message.content:
Let the projection of \(\mathbf a\) onto the plane \(P=\operatorname{span}(\mathbf b,\mathbf c)\) be

\[
\mathbf x=p\mathbf b+q\mathbf c.
\]

Since \(\mathbf a-\mathbf x\) is perpendicular to \(P\), it is perpendicular to both \(\mathbf b\) and \(\mathbf c\). Therefore,

\[
\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf x=\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf b,\qquad
\mathbf c\cdot \mathbf x=\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf c.
\]

We are given:

\[
\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf b=\frac15,\qquad
\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf c=\frac16,\qquad
\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf c=\cos 60^\circ=\frac12.
\]

Also \(\mathbf b,\mathbf c\) are unit vectors, so

\[
\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf b=1,\qquad \mathbf c\cdot \mathbf c=1.
\]

Thus,

\[
\mathbf b\cdot (p\mathbf b+q\mathbf c)
=p+q(\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c)
=p+\frac12q=\frac15,
\]

and

\[
\mathbf c\cdot (p\mathbf b+q\mathbf c)
=p(\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c)+q
=\frac12p+q=\frac16.
\]

So we solve

\[
\begin{cases}
p+\frac12q=\frac15,\\[4pt]
\frac12p+q=\frac16.
\end{cases}
\]

From the first equation,

\[
p=\frac15-\frac12q.
\]

Substitute into the second:

\[
\frac12\left(\frac15-\frac12q\right)+q=\frac16.
\]

\[
\frac1{10}-\frac14q+q=\frac16.
\]

\[
\frac1{10}+\frac34q=\frac16.
\]

\[
\frac34q=\frac16-\frac1{10}=\frac1{15}.
\]

\[
q=\frac{4}{45}.
\]

Then

\[
p=\frac15-\frac12\cdot\frac{4}{45}
=\frac15-\frac{2}{45}
=\frac{9}{45}-\frac{2}{45}
=\frac{7}{45}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
(p,q)=\left(\frac{7}{45},\frac{4}{45}\right).
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\left(\frac{7}{45},\frac{4}{45}\right)}\).
